subject.title: feat(gateway): idempotent start, non-interactive stop guard, unified lifecycle audit

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the new fail-closed non-interactive Gateway lifecycle policy for all supported automation, with every owned script migrated to an explicit `--force` consent boundary?
rationale: This PR deliberately changes a public CLI automation contract and introduces operational consent semantics; the mechanical defects are fixable, but the permanent policy and supported automation boundary need explicit maintainer acceptance.

options.title: Adopt guarded automation
options.body: Keep the policy, update every owned non-interactive stop caller to pass explicit consent, and land the repair/audit-environment fixes with runtime proof.

options.title: Limit the guard to direct user shells
options.body: Preserve existing trusted automation behavior through a narrowly documented internal path while retaining protections for untrusted non-interactive invocation.

options.title: Pause the policy change
options.body: Keep the idempotence and audit work separate until lifecycle consent semantics have a narrower approved design.

recommendation.title: Adopt guarded automation
recommendation.body: Keep the policy, update every owned non-interactive stop caller to pass explicit consent, and land the repair/audit-environment fixes with runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned author is the only concrete lifecycle-policy routing signal available in the supplied history.
